name: Mythic Sphinx, Criosphinx
body:
Mythic Criosphinx
CR 9/MR 4

This creature has the wings of a bird, the body of a lion, and the head of a ram with sad, wise eyes.

XP 6,400
N Large magical beast (mythic)
Init +0; Senses all-around vision, darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +10

DEFENSE

AC 24, touch 9, flat-footed 24 (+15 natural, –1 size)
hp 125 (10d10+70)
Fort +10, Ref +7, Will +6; +2 vs. fear effects Defensive Abilities unassailable arrogancemma; DR 5/epic

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 60 ft. (poor)
Melee 2 claws +15 (1d6+6), gore +16 (2d4+6/19-20/x3)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks bowling blow M, mythic power (4/day, surge +1d8), swooping charge (gore, 4d6+12)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 10th; concentration +12)

Constant—speak with animals, undetectable alignment At Will—augury, charm animal (DC 13)
3/day—glibness, invisibility (self only), scrying (DC 16)
1/week—commune, geas/quest

STATISTICS

Str 23, Dex 10, Con 17, Int 12, Wis 12, Cha 15
Base Atk +10; CMB +17; CMD 27 (31 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Bull Rush, Improved Critical (gore)MF, Power Attack MF, Skill Focus (Intimidate), Weapon Focus (gore)
Skills Bluff +12, Fly +1, Intimidate +18, Perception +10
Languages Common, Sphinx; speak with animals
SQ consume wealthM, sphinx-lust M

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Bowling Blow (Ex)

Whenever a mythic criosphinx successfully hits a creature with its gore attack as part of a charge, it can expend 1 use of mythic power. If it does, it may immediately make a bull rush attempt against that creature as a free action. The mythic criosphinx gains a +1 bonus on the combat maneuver check for this bull rush for every 10 feet of movement travelled as part of the charge, but its total movement for the charge (both before and after the bull rush) is still limited to twice its movement speed.

If the bull rush is successful, the target suffers an additional 1d6 points of damage for every 5 feet it was pushed, and falls prone in the square it ends its movement in.

Consume Wealth (Su)

While all criosphinxes desire valuables, mythic criosphinxes regularly consume gold, gems, and magic items, drawing power from this strange and gluttonous act. A mythic criosphinx can make a disarm or steal combat maneuver in place of one of its claw attacks, and doing so does not provoke attacks of opportunity. As a standard action, a mythic criosphinx can consume up to 2,000 coins, 20 gems, or a single object of Small size or smaller (this allows it to consume one-handed weapons made for Medium creatures). If it does, it immediately gains 1 use of mythic power for every 2,000 gp in the market price for the consumed item or items. This can allow it to have more uses of mythic power than its normal daily alotment, but any remaining uses are lost the next time it rests and regains its daily uses of mythic power. Coins and gems consumed in this way are destroyed. Objects that are consumed in this way gain the broken condition but can be recovered from the mythic criosphinx’s stomach after it is killed, provided it is recovered within one week (after which time it is destroyed completely).

Sphinx-Lust (Ex)

A mythic criosphinx is particularly affected by the presence of gynosphinxes and other intelligent, female, leonine creatures (potentially including female chimeras, manticores, and awakened or otherwise intelligent lions). As long as the mythic criosphinx is within 60 feet of such a creature, it gains a +2 morale bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, ability checks, skill checks, and saving throws. However, the mythic criosphinx is also more susceptible to suggestions from such creatures, and any creature matching this description (subject to GM discretion) gains a +5 bonus on all Bluff, Diplomacy, and Intimidate checks made against the mythic criosphinx, and the saving throw DC of any charm or compulsion effects such creatures use against the mythic criosphinx increases by +2.

Swooping Charge (Ex)

A charging mythic criosphinx deals 4d4+12 points of damage with its gore attack. A flying criosphinx who drops at least 20 feet in altitude as part of a charge deals 6d4+18 points instead.

Unassailable Arrogance (Ex)

A mythic criosphinx’s certainty in its own superiority shields it from mental assaults. A mythic criosphinx gains a bonus equal to its Charisma modifier on Will saving throws. This bonus is doubled for saving throws made to resist fear effects. Additionally, the DC for all Intimidate checks made against the mythic criosphinx increase by +10.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts or hills
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Perhaps the least leonine of all sphinxes, the ram-headed criosphinxes are always male, with curling horns crowning their heads and shaggy coats of thick, almost woolly fur on their muscular bodies. Their claws are still deadly sharp, however, and while omnivorous and using their horns to strike foe into submission rather than their jaws, they are nonetheless do crave the taste of meat above the crude subsistence that a plant diet affords them.

Criosphinxes crave wealth over nearly all other things, habitually extorting tolls for safe passage from any who pass their lands. Groups who cannot pay must yield one of their number or a pair of mounts for the criosphinx’s meal—single travelers must fight or die. Unlike many sphinxes, no mere riddle suffices—only the shine of metal or the gleam of jewels can satisfy a criosphinx. Little can convince a criosphinx to part with even a single coin save the lust that its kind bears for female sphinxes.

They lack the intellect of other sphinxes, though they fear and respect androsphinxes (or any male sphinx that seems stronger than themselves) while they disdain and lust after female sphinxes. They detest the dim-witted hieracosphinxes, regarding them as little more than beasts and a disgrace to their noble race. They drive them off whenever encountered, mock charging them to intimidate and then attacking if their falcon-headed cousins do not retreat.

Some criosphinxes set themselves as soothsayers of the desert, trading upon the storied wisdom of other sphinxes to deceive gullible travelers. Like their more blustering brethren, they seek wealth from passersby, but for the purposes of dispensing information rather than in exchange for safe passage.

Such reliable information as they possess usually comes from idle conversation with the creatures of the desert, with criosphinxes using their inborn ability to speak with animals. A criosphinx lacking in sound information usually fabricates a pleasing lie.

Criosphinxes crave mating with female sphinxes above all else, and pay well for the whereabouts of one, or better yet, a well-crafted riddle that might impress one. For their part, most other sphinxes prefer to have little to do with criosphinxes (whom they often mock as the “sheep of sphinxes”), though some few have been known to engage in brief assignations with them in the rare event a criosphinx manages to impress them with wealth or wit.
